In [[mathematics]], the '''Toronto function''' is a modification of the [[confluent hypergeometric function]] defined by A. H. Heatley as{{sfnp|Heatley|1943}}{{sfnp|Heatley|1964}}

:<math>T(m,n,r)=r^{2n-m+1}e^{-r^2}\frac{\Gamma\big(\frac 1{2}m+\frac 1{2}\big)}{\Gamma(n+1)}{}_1F_1\big({\textstyle\frac 1{2}}m+{\textstyle\frac 1{2}};n+1;r^2\big),</math>

where <math>\Gamma</math> is the [[gamma function]] and <math>_1F_1</math> is a confluent hypergeometric function [[confluent hypergeometric function#Kummer's equation|of the first kind]]. 

The Toronto function has appeared in a study on the theory of turbulence.{{sfnp|Heatley|1965}}
